07 / 11.04.2025 Heard the parties.

Apprehending his arrest, the petitioners have moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail in connection with C. C. Case No. 1426 of 2023 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 406, 467, 469, 506, 120B of the Indian Penal Code.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the allegation against the petitioners is that the petitioner no. 1 took Rs. 60,000/- from the complainant for selling a land but sold the land to the petitioner no. 2, who is the wife of the petitioner no. 1.

It is then submitted that the allegations against the petitioners are all false and the claim of the informant is hopelessly barred by time,
hence, this false case has been foisted to harass the petitioners.
The petitioners have not entered into any agreement with the complainant nor received any money.
It is next submitted that the petitioners are ready to co-operate with the trial of the case and also undertakes to furnish sufficient security including cash security.
It is further submitted by learned counsel for the petitioners that the dispute between the parties is at best a civil dispute and cloak of criminal case has been given.

It is next submitted that the complainant has suppressed the material fact that the petitioner no. 1 is Sanjay Kumar Tulsyan @ Sanjay Kumar ... vs The State Of Jharkhand on 11 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/677743/
1 the maternal uncles of her husband and the petitioner no. 2 is the wife of the petitioner no. 1 and they undertake not to annoy or disturb the informant in any manner during pendency of the case hence, the petitioners be given the privilege of anticipatory bail.

sentences.text: The learned Addl. PP opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner.
Considering aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to grant the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioners.

Hence, in the event of arrest by the police or surrender within a period of six weeks from the date of this order, the petitioners shall be released on bail on depositing Rs. 10,000/- each as cash security and on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned JMFC,
Seraikella in connection with C. C. Case No. 1426 of 2023 subject to the condition that the petitioners will co-operate with the trial of the case along with the other conditions laid down under section 482 (2) of BNSS, 2023.
(ANIL KUMAR CHOUDHARY, J.) Smita/-
